title: Power Systems
summary: The biggest Electrical topic (~12 questions). Classic repeats: Ferranti, corona, skin effect, ACSR/hollow conductors, surge impedance, insulators, per-unit, load/demand/diversity factor, HVDC, hydropower.
definitions: Receiving-end voltage exceeds sending-end voltage on long lightly loaded lines, due to line charging current.
Ionisation of air around a conductor when surface field exceeds air breakdown (≈30 kV/cm peak, 21.1 kV/cm rms).
AC current crowds near the conductor surface, raising effective resistance; grows with f, diameter and μ.
Non-uniform current distribution due to the field of nearby conductors.
Z_c = √(L/C); ≈400 Ω for overhead lines, 40–60 Ω for cables.
Surge impedance loading: load at which reactive power generated by C equals that absorbed by L (flat voltage).
V_string / (n × V of disc nearest the conductor).
Sum of individual maximum demands ÷ maximum demand of the group (≥ 1).
Slack: |V|, δ given. PV (generator): P, |V| given. PQ (load): P, Q given.
formulas: P = (V_s V_r / X) sin δ;  P_max at δ = 90°
P = ρ g Q H η  ≈ 9.81 Q H η kW
P_loss = 3I²R,  I = P/(√3 V cos φ)
Loss ∝ 1/V² (for same P, pf, conductor); conductor volume ∝ 1/V²
g = V/(x ln(R/r)), max at conductor surface; economical when R/r = e
facts: Ferranti effect is due to line capacitance (charging current); controlled by shunt reactors.
Corona: reduced by larger diameter and bundled conductors; worse in rain/fog; advantage — reduces surge steepness.
Skin effect is absent on DC; reduced by stranded conductors; hollow/ACSR conductors used in EHV.
ACSR: aluminium for conductivity, steel core for tensile strength.
Pin insulators up to 33 kV; suspension (disc) above 33 kV; strain insulators at dead ends and sharp turns.
Disc nearest the line conductor has the highest voltage; guard (grading) ring improves string efficiency.
Short line < ~80 km, medium ~80–250 km, long > ~250 km.
Transposition balances line inductance/capacitance among phases.
Series capacitors raise power-transfer capability; shunt reactors control light-load overvoltage.
HVDC: no charging current, no skin effect, no stability limit, asynchronous links; costly converters and harmonics. Break-even ~600–800 km overhead.
Turbines: Pelton (high head, impulse), Francis (medium head), Kaplan (low head, adjustable blades). Surge tank protects against water hammer.
Newton–Raphson load flow converges quadratically (fewer iterations) vs Gauss–Seidel.
Reactive power flows toward lower voltage magnitude; real power flows toward lagging angle.
Economic dispatch: equal incremental fuel cost (λ). Kelvin's law: most economical conductor size.
traps: Diversity factor is ≥ 1 and demand factor is ≤ 1 — candidates swap them.
Doubling voltage cuts losses to ¼, not ½.
Z_base uses kV² / MVA — line-to-line kV with 3-phase MVA.
SIL is V²/Z_c with V in kV gives MW directly (220²/400 = 121 MW).
Ferranti is NOT caused by resistance or inductance alone — it needs charging (capacitive) current.
